objects.description: Placeholder empty type used where a concrete type is required syntactically but no data/behavior is needed.
Enumeration identifying positional argument indices (0 through 4). Commonly used as a template parameter or tag to reference a specific argument position.
Enumeration of assignment/accumulation operation kinds: set-to, add-to, and remove-to (subtract). Useful to parametrize algorithms with an accumulation policy.
Incomplete tag type used for diagnostics when a return type is not defined. Only forward-declared in this header; no definition here.

functions.name: pinocchio::scalar_cast
functions.signature:
template <typename To, typename From>
To pinocchio::scalar_cast(const From & value)
functions.description: Converts a value of type From to type To using ScalarCast<To,From>::cast(value). By default, ScalarCast performs a static_cast<To>(value); library/users may specialize ScalarCast for custom conversion behavior. Typical usage is numeric scalar conversions or adapting scalar types across the library.
requirements: Types To and From must make ScalarCast<To,From>::cast(value) a valid expression.
If no ScalarCast<To,From> specialization is provided, static_cast<To>(value) must be well-formed for From to To.
Argument value must refer to a valid From object; it is not modified.
Function is header-only, pure, and does not manage errors; callers should ensure conversions are meaningful (e.g., consider narrowing/precision loss if applicable).

functions.name: pinocchio::ModelTpl::cast
functions.signature:
template<typename NewScalar>
typename CastType<NewScalar, ModelTpl<_Scalar, _Options, JointCollectionTpl>>::type cast() const;
functions.description: Casts this ModelTpl to an equivalent model with a different scalar type (e.g., double -> float). Use to change underlying numeric precision while preserving topology and parameters.
requirements: Must be called on a valid, initialized ModelTpl instance.
Resulting model has same structure; only scalar type changes.
All model contents must be representable in NewScalar (potential precision loss).

functions.name: pinocchio::ModelTpl::operator==

functions.description: Compares two ModelTpl instances for structural and parameter equality. Returns true if models are equal.
requirements: Both models must be valid.
Equality criteria follow ModelTpl implementation (unknown exact fields compared; expected to include topology, parameters, sizes).

functions.name: pinocchio::ModelTpl::operator!=
functions.signature: bool operator!=(const ModelTpl<_Scalar, _Options, JointCollectionTpl> & other) const;
functions.description: Logical negation of operator==. Returns true when the models are not equal.
requirements: Same requirements as operator==.
Relies on operator== for semantics.

functions.name: pinocchio::ModelTpl::addJoint
functions.description: Adds a joint to the kinematic tree with infinite bounds. Does not create a corresponding Frame entry. The inertia supported by the joint is set to Zero. Joints must be added in depth-first order.
requirements: parent must be a valid existing JointIndex in this model.
joint_placement is the placement of the new joint in the parent joint frame.
joint_name may be empty (a random name may be assigned).
Joints must be added to the tree in a depth-first order (as documented).
This method does not add a Frame; if needed, call addJointFrame separately.

functions.name: pinocchio::ModelTpl::addJoint
functions.description: Adds a joint to the kinematic tree and sets effort/velocity limits and configuration bounds.
requirements: All requirements from the simpler addJoint overload apply.
max_effort size must match the joint’s torque dimension (inferred from naming and typical API).
max_velocity size must match the joint’s velocity dimension (inferred).
min_config and max_config sizes must match the joint’s configuration dimension (inferred).
min_config must be component-wise <= max_config (inferred semantic of bounds).

functions.name: pinocchio::ModelTpl::addJoint
functions.description: Adds a joint to the kinematic tree, sets limits and configuration bounds, and initializes friction and damping parameters.
requirements: All requirements from the previous addJoint overloads apply.
friction size must match the joint’s velocity/torque dimension (inferred).
damping size must match the joint’s velocity/torque dimension (inferred).

functions.name: pinocchio::ModelTpl::addJointFrame
functions.signature: FrameIndex addJointFrame(const JointIndex & joint_index, int previous_frame_index = -1);
functions.description: Adds a frame corresponding to an existing joint into the frame tree. If previous_frame_index is negative, the parent frame is the frame of the parent joint.
requirements: joint_index must refer to an existing joint in the model.
If previous_frame_index >= 0, it must be a valid existing frame index.
If previous_frame_index < 0, the parent frame is taken as the parent joint’s frame.

functions.name: pinocchio::ModelTpl::appendBodyToJoint
functions.description: Appends a rigid body (inertia) to the specified joint in the kinematic tree. The inertia is placed relative to the joint by body_placement.
requirements: joint_index must be a valid existing joint.
Y must represent a valid spatial inertia.
body_placement is the transform from the joint frame to the body frame; defaults to identity.

functions.name: pinocchio::ModelTpl::addBodyFrame
functions.description: Adds a body frame to the frame tree under a given parent joint. The frame is located by body_placement relative to the parent joint. If parentFrame is negative, the parent frame is the frame of the parent joint.
requirements: parentJoint must be a valid existing joint index.
body_name should identify the body; uniqueness is recommended to avoid ambiguity (inferred from naming).
If parentFrame >= 0, it must be a valid existing frame index.
body_placement defaults to identity (no offset).

functions.name: pinocchio::ModelTpl::getBodyId
functions.signature: FrameIndex getBodyId(const std::string & name) const;
functions.description: Returns the frame index of a body by name. If no body is found, returns the current number of frames (nframes at time of call).
requirements: Caller must check the return value: if it equals the current number of frames, the body was not found (as warned).
Do not assume the not-found sentinel remains invalid if the model is later expanded.

functions.name: pinocchio::ModelTpl::existBodyName
functions.signature: bool existBodyName(const std::string & name) const;
functions.description: Checks if a body with the specified name exists in the model.
requirements: Name matching is exact and case-sensitive (inferred typical behavior).

functions.name: pinocchio::ModelTpl::getJointId
functions.signature: JointIndex getJointId(const std::string & name) const;
functions.description: Returns the index of a joint by name. If no joint is found, returns the current number of joints (njoints at time of call).
requirements: Caller must check the return value: if it equals the current number of joints, the joint was not found (as warned).
Do not reuse the sentinel value after model expansion.

functions.name: pinocchio::ModelTpl::existJointName
functions.signature: bool existJointName(const std::string & name) const;
functions.description: Checks if a joint with the specified name exists in the model.
requirements: Name matching is exact and case-sensitive (inferred typical behavior).

functions.name: pinocchio::ModelTpl::getFrameId
functions.signature:
FrameIndex getFrameId(const std::string & name,
                       const FrameType & type = (FrameType)(JOINT | FIXED_JOINT | BODY | OP_FRAME | SENSOR)) const;
functions.description: Returns the index of a frame with the given name and optional type mask. If no frame is found, returns the current number of frames (frames.size() at time of call).
requirements: If using the type parameter, it should be a valid FrameType or bitmask of types.
Caller must check for the not-found sentinel (index equal to frames.size() at call time).

functions.name: pinocchio::ModelTpl::existFrame
functions.signature:
bool existFrame(const std::string & name,
                 const FrameType & type = (FrameType)(JOINT | FIXED_JOINT | BODY | OP_FRAME | SENSOR)) const;
functions.description: Checks if a frame with the specified name (and optional type filter) exists.
requirements: If using the type parameter, it should be a valid FrameType or bitmask of types.

functions.name: pinocchio::ModelTpl::addFrame
functions.signature: FrameIndex addFrame(const Frame & frame, const bool append_inertia = true);
functions.description: Adds a Frame to the model’s frame tree. If append_inertia is true, the frame’s inertia is added to the inertia supported by its parent joint. If the frame already exists, returns its index.
requirements: frame must reference a valid parent joint (frame.parentJoint) present in the model.
If append_inertia is true, the Frame must carry a valid inertia; it will be accumulated onto the joint’s supported inertia.

bool check(const AlgorithmCheckerBase<D> & checker = AlgorithmCheckerBase<D>()) const;
functions.description: Validates this model against a provided algorithm checker. Returns true if the model satisfies the checker’s conditions.
requirements: checker must implement checkModel(const ModelTpl&).
Model must be initialized.

functions.name: pinocchio::ModelTpl::check
functions.signature: bool check() const;
functions.description: Runs the default suite of model checks (DEFAULT_CHECKERS). Returns true if the model is valid.
requirements: Model must be initialized.
Default checkers must be available in the build (as per library configuration).

functions.name: pinocchio::ModelTpl::hasConfigurationLimit
functions.signature: std::vector<bool> hasConfigurationLimit();
functions.description: Reports per-configuration-element whether a configuration limit exists. Returns a boolean vector of size model.nq.
requirements: Model.nq must be up-to-date with current joint set.

functions.name: pinocchio::ModelTpl::hasConfigurationLimitInTangent
functions.signature: std::vector<bool> hasConfigurationLimitInTangent();
functions.description: Reports per-velocity-space element whether a configuration limit applies in tangent space. Returns a boolean vector of size model.nq.
requirements: Model.nq must be up-to-date with current joint set.

functions.name: pinocchio::DataTpl::DataTpl
functions.signature:
template<typename _Scalar, int _Options, template<typename, int> class JointCollectionTpl>
explicit pinocchio::DataTpl<_Scalar, _Options, JointCollectionTpl>::DataTpl(const pinocchio::ModelTpl<_Scalar, _Options, JointCollectionTpl> & model);
functions.description: Constructs a DataTpl instance sized and initialized for a given Pinocchio model. Intended to allocate and prepare all runtime buffers (kinematics/dynamics intermediates, Jacobians, mass matrices, etc.) consistent with the provided model. Typical usage: create a ModelTpl, then construct DataTpl with that model before calling Pinocchio algorithms that fill/use Data.
requirements: The model argument must be a pinocchio::ModelTpl<_Scalar, _Options, JointCollectionTpl> with template parameters matching this DataTpl instantiation (compile-time requirement).
The provided model should represent a valid rigid-body system; sizes and indexing must be coherent with the model (implied by usage; details not further specified in the header).
Callers should use this constructor (rather than the default one) when they need all internal buffers to be properly sized to the model before running algorithms.

functions.name: pinocchio::DataTpl::DataTpl
functions.signature:
template<typename _Scalar, int _Options, template<typename, int> class JointCollectionTpl>
pinocchio::DataTpl<_Scalar, _Options, JointCollectionTpl>::DataTpl();
functions.description: Default constructor for DataTpl. Creates an empty/uninitialized data container without sizing its internal buffers to any model. Primarily useful for deferred initialization, placement-new, or serialization frameworks. Most algorithms expect a Data sized for a specific model, so this constructor is typically followed by assignment or reconstruction with a model.
requirements: Constructs an instance without associating it to a model; internal buffers are not guaranteed to be sized. Callers must not use this Data with algorithms that expect model-sized buffers until it is properly initialized/sized (e.g., by constructing with a model or assigning from an already-initialized Data).

functions.name: pinocchio::updateGlobalPlacements
functions.description: Updates all joints' global placements (data.oMi) using the current relative joint placements stored in data. Typical usage: call after algorithms (e.g., rnea, aba) that may have updated relative joint transforms to refresh the absolute/world placements without re-running full forward kinematics.
requirements: model and data must refer to the same kinematic model instance (constructed/paired together).
data must contain valid, up-to-date relative joint placements required for propagation (e.g., data.liMi or equivalent as maintained by algorithms such as rnea/aba).
Caller must expect data.oMi to be overwritten/updated for all joints.
model must be a valid articulated model (joint hierarchy well-formed).

functions.name: pinocchio::forwardKinematics
functions.description: Computes forward kinematics from configuration only: updates joint placements in data based on q. Use when only poses are needed.
requirements: model and data must refer to the same model instance.
q must be a configuration vector of size model.nq and represent a valid configuration for the model.
Data fields holding placements will be overwritten/updated.
ConfigVectorType must be an Eigen-compatible vector type (MatrixBase).

functions.name: pinocchio::getRelativePlacement
functions.description: Returns the pose of jointIdTarget relative to jointIdRef, expressed in the selected convention. Requires forwardKinematics to have been run so that data contains up-to-date placements. WORLD uses data.oMi (O(1)); LOCAL uses data.liMi (O(n)) and should be used consistently with algorithms run in LOCAL convention.
requirements: model and data must refer to the same model instance.
forwardKinematics must have been called beforehand to update placements in data.
jointIdRef and jointIdTarget must be valid joint indices in model.
convention must be a valid Convention enum; if Convention::LOCAL is used, the rest of the pipeline (e.g., aba/crba) should also be in LOCAL convention as per the note.
This function does not modify data.

functions.name: pinocchio::getVelocity
functions.description: Returns the spatial velocity of the specified joint expressed in the selected reference frame. Requires first- or second-order forwardKinematics to have been run to populate velocities in data.
requirements: model and data must refer to the same model instance.
First- or second-order forwardKinematics (with q,v or q,v,a) must have been called beforehand to update velocities in data.
jointId must be a valid joint index in model.
rf must be a valid pinocchio::ReferenceFrame value (e.g., LOCAL or WORLD).
This function does not modify data.

functions.name: pinocchio::getAcceleration
functions.description: Returns the spatial acceleration of the specified joint expressed in the selected reference frame. Requires second-order forwardKinematics to have been run to populate accelerations in data.
requirements: model and data must refer to the same model instance.
Second-order forwardKinematics (with q,v,a) must have been called beforehand to update accelerations in data.
jointId must be a valid joint index in model.
rf must be a valid pinocchio::ReferenceFrame value (e.g., LOCAL or WORLD).
This function does not modify data.

functions.name: pinocchio::getClassicalAcceleration
functions.description: Returns the classical (i.e., spatial acceleration with centrifugal/coriolis terms accounted for) acceleration of the specified joint in the selected reference frame. Requires second-order forwardKinematics to have been run.
requirements: model and data must refer to the same model instance.
Second-order forwardKinematics (with q,v,a) must have been called beforehand to update accelerations in data.
jointId must be a valid joint index in model.
rf must be a valid pinocchio::ReferenceFrame value (e.g., LOCAL or WORLD).
This function does not modify data.
